title: AI-Augmented Medical Coding
outcome: Review AI-generated clinical records and codes as an expert exception-handler — catching the gap between standards-compliant and clinically correct, and escalating before harm reaches a patient.

phases.name: Reviewer, Not Data-Entry Clerk
phases.outcome: Understand what AI clinical coding pipelines do, what they get wrong, and what the human reviewer is actually for.

modules.name: What This Role Actually Is
modules.objective: Describe the reviewer role in an AI-assisted coding pipeline and how it differs from manual coding.
lessons: The pipeline codes; you handle what it can't
A day in the queue: what actually reaches a reviewer
Why this role exists and isn't going away
What you are accountable for when you approve
Working this role from bed, honestly
practice: Sort eight queue items by whether a reviewer is needed
lab: Shadow a queue: triage twenty items and log your reasoning
A triage log with an approve/correct/escalate call and reason per item

modules.name: Reading Clinical Documentation
modules.objective: Read a clinical note well enough to tell what actually happened to the patient.
lessons: Anatomy of a note: chief complaint to plan
Abbreviations, and the ones that mean two things
Ruled out, suspected, history of: the words that change the code
Templates, copy-forward, and text that stopped being true
What the note doesn't say, and why that matters
practice: Extract the encounter facts from eight notes
lab: Summarise five real-shaped notes into codable facts
A fact sheet per note, with anything ambiguous flagged as a query

modules.name: The Coding Systems
modules.objective: Navigate ICD, CPT/procedure and drug terminologies well enough to check somebody else's choice.
lessons: ICD-10-CM: structure, specificity and the last character
Procedure coding and what counts as one procedure
SNOMED CT, LOINC and RxNorm: what each is for
Code sets change: versions, effective dates and the wrong-year code
Looking a code up properly instead of pattern-matching
practice: Verify eight code selections against the source note
lab: Build your own reference card for your top codes
A reference card for the twenty codes you'd see most, with their specificity traps

modules.name: How the AI Assigns a Code
modules.objective: Explain how an automated coding pipeline reaches a code, so you can predict where it will fail.
lessons: From note text to candidate codes: the pipeline stages
Confidence scores and what they don't mean
Why it prefers common codes over correct ones
Negation and the pipeline that misses a "not"
Where in the pipeline your correction actually lands
practice: Predict the pipeline's error for eight note types
lab: Characterise one pipeline's failure profile from its output
A failure profile naming at least five recurring error types with examples

modules.name: The Reviewer's Own Failure Mode
modules.objective: Recognise and counter the drift toward approving whatever the system suggests.
lessons: Automation bias: why usually-right is dangerous
What a real check looks like versus what a fast one looks like
Fatigue, volume targets and the quality curve
Building a personal check routine that survives a bad day
practice: Spot the rubber-stamp in eight review records
lab: Audit your own first fifty reviews
A self-audit naming your own error pattern and the routine change that addresses it

phases.name: Validating Against Real Standards
phases.outcome: Check records against HL7, FHIR, terminology and privacy requirements — for logic, not just for completeness.

modules.name: HL7 and FHIR in Practice
modules.objective: Read a FHIR resource and tell whether it says what the clinical record says.
lessons: Why standards exist: the message that has to survive the trip
FHIR resources: Patient, Encounter, Condition, Observation
References between resources, and the broken ones
Reading a v2 message when that's what the system speaks
practice: Validate eight resources against their source notes
lab: Review a FHIR bundle against the encounter it describes
A review naming every discrepancy between bundle and record

modules.name: Structurally Complete, Clinically Wrong
modules.objective: Find the records that pass every automated validator and still misdescribe the patient.
lessons: The validator checks shape, not truth
Right code, wrong laterality, wrong encounter
Codes that contradict each other in one record
Sequencing: which diagnosis is principal and why it matters
Records that are internally consistent and clinically impossible
practice: Find the clinical contradiction in eight valid records
lab: Review a batch that passed validation for clinical sense
A findings list with the clinical reason each flagged record is wrong

modules.name: Terminology Mapping and Its Traps
modules.objective: Judge whether a mapping between terminologies preserved the clinical meaning.
lessons: Mapping is lossy, and the loss is where harm hides
One-to-many maps and the choice somebody made
Granularity loss: the specific finding becoming a general one
Local codes, legacy systems, and the mapping table nobody owns
Checking a map against the source, not the target
practice: Assess eight mappings for meaning loss
lab: Audit a mapping table for clinically significant loss
An audit naming each lossy mapping and its clinical consequence

modules.name: HIPAA, Minimum Necessary and Real Privacy
modules.objective: Judge whether a record's handling meets privacy requirements in practice, not just on paper.
lessons: Identifiers, and the free text that re-identifies
Minimum necessary as an actual working rule
What may be sent to an AI vendor, and under what agreement
Access, audit trails and who looked at this record
practice: Judge eight disclosure scenarios
lab: Privacy-review a de-identified dataset
A review naming every residual re-identification risk you found

modules.name: Documentation Integrity and Compliance
modules.objective: Recognise coding patterns that create compliance exposure, whoever or whatever produced them.
lessons: Upcoding, and how a pipeline arrives at it innocently
Unbundling and the modifier that shouldn't be there
Documentation that doesn't support the code billed
Query the clinician: when, and how to write one
Audit trails: making your own review defensible
practice: Flag the compliance risk in eight coded encounters
lab: Write clinician queries for five ambiguous encounters
Five non-leading queries that would stand up in an audit

phases.name: Catching What the AI Misses
phases.outcome: Recognise, by pattern, the encounters where automated coding is most likely to be confidently wrong.

modules.name: The Shape of a Confident Error
modules.objective: Predict which encounters a pipeline will get wrong while reporting high confidence.
lessons: High confidence, wrong answer: why they co-occur
The note that reads like a different note
Rare diagnoses and the training data that lacks them
practice: Predict confidence-versus-correctness for eight encounters
lab: Assemble a watch list from real error data
A watch list of at least ten encounter patterns, each with a real example

modules.name: Comorbidity and Complexity
modules.objective: Code encounters where several conditions interact and the pipeline treats them as independent.
lessons: Multiple chronic conditions in one encounter
Manifestation and etiology: codes that must travel together
The condition being treated versus the condition present
Severity, acuity and the modifiers that carry them
practice: Code eight multi-condition encounters and justify sequencing
lab: Review a complex chronic-care batch
A corrected batch with the clinical reasoning behind each re-sequencing

modules.name: Conditions the System Handles Badly
modules.objective: Code conditions that are poorly represented, contested, or historically dismissed — accurately.
lessons: Diagnoses that took the patient years to get
Dysautonomia, ME/CFS, fibromyalgia: coding what exists
Symptom codes versus diagnosis codes, and what each costs a patient
Language in notes that dismisses, and how it propagates into data
Long COVID and conditions the code set caught up with late
practice: Code eight encounters for poorly-represented conditions
lab: Audit a set of records for dismissive coding patterns
An audit naming each pattern, its downstream effect, and the correct coding

modules.name: Populations With Their Own Rules
modules.objective: Apply the coding rules that change entirely for specific populations.
lessons: Neonatal and pediatric coding: different rules, not adjusted ones
Obstetric encounters and the trimester that changes the code
Geriatric encounters, polypharmacy and functional status
Behavioural health and the documentation that supports it
Where population rules and pipelines collide
practice: Code eight population-specific encounters
lab: Review a mixed-population batch for rule misapplication
A corrected batch with the population rule cited per correction

modules.name: Escalating Before Harm
modules.objective: Know what to escalate, to whom, how fast, and how to write it so it gets acted on.
lessons: The difference between a correction and an escalation
Systemic error: when one wrong record means a thousand
Writing an escalation a busy clinical lead will act on
Escalating when you're new, remote and unsure
What to do when the escalation is ignored
practice: Decide escalate or correct for eight findings
lab: Write a systemic-error escalation
An escalation stating the pattern, the evidence, the scope and the requested action

phases.name: Patient Safety Auditing
phases.outcome: Audit AI-assisted clinical systems for safety-critical failure and write findings both clinical and engineering teams can act on.

modules.name: How Coding Errors Reach Patients
modules.objective: Trace the path from a wrong code to a harmed patient, and find where it could have been stopped.
lessons: The chain: code, record, decision support, clinician, patient
Problem lists that follow a patient for years
Allergy and medication data: the fastest path to harm
Alerts that fire on bad data, and the fatigue that follows
Where a wrong code stops being recoverable
practice: Trace eight coding errors to their clinical consequence
lab: Trace a real error to every downstream system it touched
A trace diagram naming each affected system and the earliest interception point

modules.name: Running a Safety Audit
modules.objective: Design and run an audit that finds real safety issues rather than confirming the system is fine.
lessons: Scoping an audit so it can actually be finished
Sampling for harm, not for reassurance
Severity classification that people agree on
Evidence: what you must keep for every finding
Auditing at variable capacity, in stages
practice: Scope seven audits under real constraints
lab: Run a scoped safety audit end to end
An audit with scope, method, sample, findings, severities and evidence

modules.name: Writing Findings Two Audiences Can Act On
modules.objective: Write a finding that a clinician and an engineer both understand and can act on without a meeting.
lessons: The finding nobody could act on, and why
Clinical impact and technical cause in the same paragraph
Reproduction steps for a clinical error
Severity, urgency, and not crying wolf
practice: Rewrite eight unusable findings
lab: Write the report for your audit
An audit report with an executive summary, findings, severities and owned recommendations

modules.name: Getting the System Fixed
modules.objective: Turn findings into actual changes in a pipeline, a workflow or a policy.
lessons: Why correct findings don't get fixed
Fixing the pipeline versus fixing the review step
Feeding corrections back so the same error stops recurring
Working with the vendor whose product is wrong
Verifying a fix actually fixed it
practice: Choose the intervention point for eight recurring errors
lab: Propose and verify one systemic fix
A proposal, the change made, and the before-and-after evidence

modules.name: Governance and Regulation
modules.objective: Know the regulatory frame around clinical AI well enough to work inside it and ask the right questions.
lessons: When a coding tool becomes a regulated device
Validation evidence a health system should have and often doesn't
Model updates in a regulated setting
Questions to ask before a pipeline goes live
practice: Judge the governance gap in seven deployments
lab: Write a pre-go-live governance checklist
A checklist a health system could use before enabling an AI coding pipeline

phases.name: Working at Volume
phases.outcome: Sustain accuracy and speed across a real queue, with real quality measurement and real fatigue.

lessons: Triage first: not every item deserves equal time

Batching similar items to keep context
Knowing when to stop for the day

modules.name: Measuring Your Own Accuracy
modules.objective: Know your real error rate and what kind of errors you personally make.
lessons: Accuracy rates in coding: how they're actually calculated
Your error profile is not random
Disagreement that turns out to be ambiguity
Improving one error type at a time
practice: Adjudicate eight double-coding disagreements
lab: Measure and analyse your own error profile

modules.name: Productivity, Targets and Honesty
modules.objective: Handle volume targets without letting them quietly convert into approval-without-review.
lessons: What productivity targets do to review quality

lab: Build an evidence pack for a target renegotiation

modules.name: The Tools You'll Actually Use

EHR navigation without a second monitor

phases.name: Getting and Keeping the Work

modules.name: Interviews and Coding Tests

modules.name: Accommodation and Disclosure
